objective: Resolve whether the #284 negative solve_seconds was a realtime clock artifact or telemetry corruption, without changing canonical health policy.

finding.ego_boundary_inference: EGO synchronization stalled after adapter outputs; DDS reader vs EGO callback/executor remains unresolved.

interpretation: The negative #284 sample was not reproduced in #286 or #288. In #288 all 634 positive-duration pairs were nonnegative; Ceres wall time was 17–66 microseconds shorter than the outer steady-clock interval. This confirms close agreement during this run, but cannot retrospectively identify the cause of #284. The host clock offset also remained stable during the observed runs.
qualification: Planner-only diagnostic; no trajectory execution, controller, PX4, runtime truth input, or GOAL C/D/E/F acceptance. Canonical health gate and thresholds remain unchanged and PROVISIONAL.
ego_interpretation: At EGO now=37.671–37.852 s, the EGO depth/pose sync counter remains 963 and occupancy last updated at 36.648 s. At the matching source-time window, MapStatus is still ready and forwarded_depth_count rises 984→1014, while the independent optimized-odometry subscriber receives stamps 37.621–37.819 s. Mapping closes only later with normalized_cost_exceeded; its host log timestamp is 4.044 s after the last EGO timeout (4.294 s after the first), and MapStatus remains ready through wall_elapsed 54.659 s before reset acknowledgement at 54.908 s. This places the observed stall downstream of the self-maintained mapping/localization adapter outputs and before EGO synchronized occupancy refresh; an EGO subscription/message-filter/DDS/executor issue is plausible. It does not distinguish reader delivery from EGO callback/synchronizer behavior. The later localization lock/reset did not trigger these earlier timeout messages. EGO also repeatedly rejected terminal points in its inflated obstacle map; no vehicle control was present.
